たこ焼き.summary: Balls of batter with a piece of octopus inside, the star of Osaka's flour-based street food. Crispy outside and gooey inside. Fresh takoyaki is very hot inside, so let it cool a little. Some shops serve it with dashi or soy sauce instead of sauce.
たこ焼き.area: Dotonbori, Namba and all over Osaka City

お好み焼き.summary: Osaka-style savory pancake: cabbage and toppings are mixed into the batter before grilling. Finished with sauce, mayonnaise and bonito flakes. Cut and eat it right on the hot plate with a small spatula (kote) to keep it hot.

串カツ.summary: Battered and deep-fried skewers of meat, vegetables and seafood, the local favorite of Shinsekai. You can order just one at a time. No double-dipping in the shared sauce! Use the free cabbage to scoop more sauce.

shops.name: Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai Main Store
shops.query: 串かつだるま 新世界総本店
shops.comment: The long-running shop famous for its no-double-dipping rule. Easy for first-timers.

shops.name: Tengu
shops.query: てんぐ 串かつ 新世界 ジャンジャン横丁
shops.comment: A popular spot on Janjan Yokocho, also known for its dote-yaki.

shops.name: Yaekatsu
shops.query: 八重勝 串かつ 新世界
shops.comment: A classic with a constant line, known for its light, crispy batter.

ねぎ焼き.summary: A cousin of okonomiyaki made with a mountain of green onions and a thin batter, eaten with soy sauce or ponzu for a lighter taste.

いか焼き.summary: Batter with chopped squid, pressed flat between two hot plates. A thin, chewy Osaka snack. It is a famous department store basement snack. The line moves fast.

shops.name: Hanshin Ikayaki (Hanshin Umeda Main Store)
shops.query: 阪神名物いか焼き 阪神梅田本店
shops.comment: A famous counter in the department store basement.

きつねうどん.summary: Udon topped with a large piece of sweet simmered fried tofu. The clear, light-colored kelp broth is the taste of Osaka.
きつねうどん.area: Osaka City (said to originate in Senba)

どて焼き.summary: Beef tendon slowly simmered in miso until meltingly soft. A standard side dish at kushikatsu restaurants.

肉吸い.summary: Beef udon without the noodles: a savory broth with beef and a soft-cooked egg. It started at a long-running udon shop in Namba. Order it with a small bowl of rice, the classic combination.

shops.name: Chitose Main Store
shops.query: 千とせ 本店 肉吸い
shops.comment: Known as the birthplace of nikusui.

豚まん.summary: In Osaka, pork buns are called butaman, not nikuman. Fluffy dough filled with juicy pork and onion. Eat it with a dab of mustard, Osaka style.
豚まん.area: Around Namba, Umeda and other stations in Osaka City

shops.name: 551 Horai Main Store
shops.comment: Osaka's best-known butaman. You can watch them being made at the counter.

バッテラ.summary: Pressed sushi of vinegar-cured mackerel on rice, topped with a thin sheet of kelp. The name comes from the Portuguese word for a small boat.
バッテラ.area: Sushi shops and department stores in Osaka City

鯨のハリハリ鍋.summary: A hot pot of whale meat and mizuna greens quickly cooked in broth. The name comes from the crisp "hari-hari" texture of the mizuna.
鯨のハリハリ鍋.area: Osaka City (only a few restaurants serve it)

てっちり.summary: A hot pot of pufferfish (fugu) and vegetables, a winter specialty in Osaka, which eats a lot of fugu. Finish with rice porridge in the leftover broth. Eat fugu only at specialist restaurants with licensed chefs.
てっちり.area: Dotonbori and other areas of Osaka City

うどんすき.summary: A hot pot of thick udon cooked in broth with seafood, chicken, vegetables and more. It was created by a long-established Osaka restaurant.

りくろーおじさんのチーズケーキ.summary: A fluffy cheesecake loved for being sold fresh from the oven. A bell rings when a new batch is ready, and you can watch the logo being branded on top.
りくろーおじさんのチーズケーキ.area: Shops in Namba, Umeda and elsewhere in Osaka

ミックスジュース.summary: A blend of fruit such as banana and peach with milk, a standard drink at Osaka coffee shops.
ミックスジュース.area: Coffee shops and station juice stands in Osaka City

みたらし小餅.summary: Bite-size grilled rice cakes covered in a sweet-savory soy glaze, a staple of Osaka's long-established sweet shops.

岩おこし.summary: Crushed rice bound with syrup into a very hard, crunchy sweet. A classic Osaka souvenir.
